small_guidance: The bug is in BN training: the reference computes BN over the batch (using batch statistics) then subtracts the spatial mean of the BN output. The current train kernel computes spatial_mean of the raw conv output x (not of BN(x)), then outputs (x - spatial_mean)*scale, omitting the BN shift entirely and using the wrong mean. Fix: compute y = (x - batch_mean)*scale + beta first (or equivalently fuse), then compute spatial mean of y per (n,c) and subtract. Concretely, spatial_mean_of_BN(x) = (spatial_mean(x) - batch_mean)*scale + beta; subtract this from y. Update apply kernel to output y - sm_of_bn. Keep BLOCK_SP=1024, num_warps=4.
large_guidance: If redesigning, fuse the entire BN-train + spatial-mean-subtract into a two-pass per-(n,c) kernel: pass 1 reduces sum and sumsq per (n,c); host reduces across n to get batch mean/var and computes scale=gamma/sqrt(var+eps), shift=beta-mean*scale; pass 2 streams x, computes y=x*scale+shift, accumulates spatial sum of y to get per-(n,c) spatial mean, then a third pass (or store y then subtract) writes y - spatial_mean_y. Alternatively, since spatial_mean(y) = scale*spatial_mean(x) + shift, compute it analytically from the already-collected per-(n,c) sum, avoiding a third pass. Keep conv_transpose3d kernel unchanged.
